must_haves: Standard resting 12-lead ECGs of about 10 s per recording (a set with mixed lengths counts if a large 10-s subset can be selected)
Diagnostic labels covering atrial fibrillation and conduction disorders (bundle branch blocks and AV block)
At least a few thousand labelled recordings
Downloadable this week without any application, credentialing, data use agreement or ethics approval (open access)
Preference, not a hard requirement: labels assigned or confirmed by cardiologists

A.access_stated: open download, no account, application or credentialing; CC BY 4.0
A.note: The page is open access ("Anyone can access the files, as long as they conform to the terms of the specified license", CC BY 4.0) with 21,799 10-s 12-lead records from 18,869 patients "annotated by up to two cardiologists"; scp_statements.csv lists AFIB, AFLT, CLBBB, CRBBB, ILBBB, IRBBB, LAFB, LPFB, 1AVB, 2AVB, 3AVB and IVCD, and "Records in fold 9 and 10 underwent at least one human evaluation".

A.dataset: Chapman-Shaoxing / Ningbo (PhysioNet, A large scale 12-lead electrocardiogram database for arrhythmia study)
A.note: The page is open access ("Anyone can access the files...", CC BY 4.0) with 10-s 12-lead 500 Hz ECGs of 45,152 patients, where "a licensed physician labeled the rhythm and other cardiac conditions", a second physician validated and a senior physician resolved disagreements; ConditionNames_SNOMED-CT.csv includes AFIB, AF (flutter), LBBB, RBBB, 1AVB, 2AVB and 3AVB.

The Zenodo record is open under CC BY 4.0 with 345,779 exams from 233,770 patients, 12-lead at 400 Hz ("Some signals originally have a duration of 10 seconds ... and others of 7 seconds") and labels 1dAVb, RBBB, LBBB, SB, AF and ST; the Nature Communications paper says the training labels were extracted from cardiologists' text reports and filtered against automatic Uni-G/Minnesota analysis, consistent with the answer's caveat.

A.access_stated: open on Figshare (licence to be checked on the record page)
A.note: The Figshare HTML page returned 403, so the collection was read through api.figshare.com: 25,770 12-lead 500 Hz records from 24,666 patients, CC0 items with direct file download, AHA codes including AF (50), LBBB (104), RBBB (106) and AV block (83-88), and the paper says "The responsible cardiologist made the final diagnosis"; the answer's "10 s" is imprecise because "the length of records ranges from 10 to 60 seconds" (24,242 of 25,770 are 10-15 s).

The page is open access under CC BY 4.0 with "over 88,000 ECGs shared publicly as training data" (88,253 across CPSC, CPSC-Extra, INCART, PTB, PTB-XL, Georgia, Chapman-Shaoxing and Ningbo) in SNOMED-CT, and the scored list includes AF, IAVB, LBBB and RBBB; the page gives CPSC lengths as "6-144 s" rather than the answer's 6-60 s, and it notes that some sources have human-overread machine labels.

B.note: The page is open access ("Anyone can access the files, as long as they conform to the terms of the specified license", CC BY 4.0) with 21,799 10-s 12-lead records from 18,869 patients "annotated by up to two cardiologists"; scp_statements.csv lists AFIB, CLBBB, CRBBB, ILBBB, IRBBB, 1AVB, 2AVB and 3AVB, and the answer's quotation matches the page.

B.dataset: Chapman-Shaoxing/Ningbo (PhysioNet, A large scale 12-lead electrocardiogram database for arrhythmia study)
B.note: The page is open access under CC BY 4.0 with 10-s 12-lead 500 Hz ECGs of 45,152 patients, the answer's quotations on physician labelling match it, and the label list includes AFIB, LBBB, RBBB, 1AVB, 2AVB and 3AVB; the Zenodo record 16789324 that the answer calls "a smaller Shaoxing-only copy" is not a subset, because its description points to this PhysioNet page and its single zip is the same size (2,498,709,074 bytes) as PhysioNet's full v1.0.0 archive.

The page is open access under CC BY 4.0 with training folders CPSC 6,877 and CPSC-Extra 3,453 (6-60 s), INCART 74 (30 min), PTB 516, PTB-XL 21,837 (10 s) and Georgia 10,344 (10 s, 500 Hz), 43,101 in total in SNOMED-CT, whose scored list includes AF, IAVB, LBBB and RBBB; the page also says "Some databases have human overread machine labels".

The page is open access under CC BY 4.0 with "over 88,000 ECGs shared publicly as training data" (88,253), covering all of the 2020 training sources plus Chapman-Shaoxing (10,247) and Ningbo (34,905), in SNOMED-CT, and the scored list includes AF, IAVB, LBBB and RBBB.

The Zenodo record is open under CC BY 4.0 with exactly 345,779 exams from 233,770 patients, 12-lead at 400 Hz in a mix of 7-s and 10-s traces, labelled 1dAVb, RBBB, LBBB, SB, AF and ST; the Nature Communications paper says the training labels were extracted from cardiologists' text reports and filtered against automatic Uni-G/Minnesota analysis, consistent with the answer's caveat.

The Zenodo record is open under CC BY 4.0 and contains "827 ECG tracings" annotated by two cardiologists, with "a third senior specialist" deciding disagreements, so it fails the few-thousand-recordings requirement (the answer itself offers it only as a test set).
